The NL's 'and approaches its destination' is a precondition on the state of the world, not a property of the event.

The Approaching state (line:14) has name body projections 'Nearing Destination' and 'Ready to Stop/Decelerate' but no 'Send' signal. No transition from Approaching carries a 'Send' effect.
issues.reason: The contract requires the Approaching state to emit a 'Send' signal. No such event, effect, or emission exists in the FCSTM. This is a clear missing effect with no predicate support for state-level emission checks.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The 'Send' signal might be considered informal documentation or a subsumed part of another signal (e.g., SendArrived in Arrived_Stop_SendArrived). However, the NL names it as a distinct signal 'Send' that the Approaching state emits, and no such signal exists in the model.
issues.title: Approaching state does not formally send 'Send' signal

issues.basis: FCSTM text: state Approaching named 'Approaching\n[PlantUML body] Nearing Destination\n[PlantUML body] Ready to Stop/Decelerate'; reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory count=0; source body projections trace:body:InMotion.Approaching:1 and :2.

issues.basis: NL1 establishes InMotion as the operating target; inspection-equivalent reachability shows InMotion and 4 children all unreachable; verify-fact reachability:state:InMotion:line:11 status=refuted; reference-inspection W_UNREACHABLE_STATE for InMotion.Accelerating, InMotion.Cruising, InMotion.Approaching.
issues.expected: InMotion is reachable from the root initial entry via the path [*] -> DoorsClosing -> InMotion.
issues.observed: InMotion (state:InMotion:line:11) is unreachable from root initial entry. The only path to InMotion is through DoorsClosing (transition:line:35), but DoorsClosing itself is unreachable. Verify-fact confirms reachability refuted.
issues.reason: InMotion is the main operating composite described in NL4-NL10. Its unreachability from root is a distinct global reachability property from the local initial_entry defect. The verify-fact explicitly refutes reachability for InMotion and all its children.
issues.requirement_quote: The system starts in the DoorsClosing state and transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If the root initial entry were corrected to target DoorsClosing, InMotion would become reachable via transition:line:35. The unreachability is entirely caused by the root initial entry defect, making this a consequence rather than an independent structural flaw in InMotion's own topology.
issues.title: InMotion operating composite is unreachable from system root

issues.basis: NL2, NL5, NL6, NL7 event-driven transition descriptions; inspection-equivalent event_consumers (6 events, all with reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); verify-facts event-consumer checks all status=refuted; diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for all 6 events.
issues.expected: Events Arrived_Stop_SendArrived, Obstacle_Detected, Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate, and Entry_Accelerate each have at least one reachable consumer transition within the InMotion operating scope.
issues.observed: All six declared events (including Closed_SendDeparted) have consumer transitions but zero reachable consumers. Inspection-equivalent event_consumers shows reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for every event. Verify-facts refute all six event-consumer checks.
issues.reason: NL2 through NL7 establish that multiple events must trigger transitions within the InMotion operating scope. The cross-view fact that no consumer of any event is reachable means the system cannot respond to any stimulus in its operational lifetime. This is a distinct operational coverage property: it captures the behavioral consequence that the system is completely non-responsive despite having all transitions declared.
issues.requirement_quote: In the InMotion state, the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal, or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The unreachability of event consumers is entirely downstream of the root initial entry defect. If the root entry were corrected, all consumers would become reachable since their transitions are correctly declared. This coverage gap is a consequence, not an independent structural omission of consumer transitions.
issues.title: All event consumers within InMotion scope are unreachable; no operational event response is possible

issues.basis: NL5 and NL8 text; FCSTM transition:line:15 (triggers=[Entry_Accelerate]); reference-inspection W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING for InMotion; verify-fact initial-entry:transition:line:15 status=refuted has_trigger=true; inspection-equivalent diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL line:15.
issues.expected: InMotion has an unconditional initial edge [*] -> Accelerating so the composite can be entered without requiring a prior trigger.
issues.observed: The only initial edge in InMotion scope (transition:line:15) targets Accelerating but carries trigger Entry_Accelerate. Reference inspection reports W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING with existing_conditional_count=1. Verify-fact initial-entry:transition:line:15 is refuted (has_trigger=true).
issues.reason: The NL5 statement 'The system begins in the Accelerating substate' implies a default entry without precondition. The FCSTM models this as a conditional initial transition requiring Entry_Accelerate to fire first. In standard state machine semantics, a conditional initial edge means the composite cannot be entered until the condition is met, which is a behavioral restriction not stated in the NL.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL8 explicitly says the entry is 'marked by the Entry/Accelerate action,' which could indicate the author intended a conditional entry. However, in FCSTM semantics a trigger on an initial edge makes the composite unenterable until that event fires, which conflicts with NL5's unqualified 'the system begins in the Accelerating substate.'
issues.title: InMotion initial entry to Accelerating is conditional; no unconditional default entry exists

issues.basis: NL10 text; FCSTM transitions:line:21 and line:24 (no guards); inspection-equivalent shows guarded_transition_count=2 only for InMotion→Stopping and InMotion→EmergencyStopping; no guard on Approaching exits.
issues.expected: The system stays in the Approaching state while the 'nearing destination' condition holds; exit is permitted only when the system is ready to stop or decelerate.
issues.observed: The Approaching state has two outgoing transitions (line:21 on Arrived_Stop_SendArrived, line:24 on Obstacle_Detected) with no guards. The system can leave Approaching whenever these events fire, regardless of whether the 'nearing destination' or 'ready to stop' condition is actually satisfied. No guard constrains the exit.
issues.reason: NL10 explicitly states a retention condition: the system must remain in Approaching 'while nearing the destination.' The FCSTM has no guard on the exit transitions that checks this condition. The frozen predicate registry has no state_retention predicate, so this remains a precise W1 candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL's 'until it is ready to stop or decelerate' could be interpreted as describing the natural exit condition (arrival at destination) rather than requiring an explicit guard. In many state machine designs, the triggering event itself implies the condition is met. The Obstacle_Detected exit could be seen as an emergency override that takes precedence over the retention condition.
issues.title: Approaching state can be exited without the 'nearing destination' retention condition being enforced

issues.basis: NL5 text; FCSTM transition:line:16 (triggers=[Reached_Cruising_Cruise], effects=[]); source inventory tr_0003 event='Reached Cruising/Cruise'.
issues.expected: The transition from Accelerating to Cruising executes the effect 'Cruise' as part of the speed-reached signal.
issues.observed: Transition:line:16 (Accelerating → Cruising, trigger Reached_Cruising_Cruise) has effects=[] (empty). The 'Cruise' component of the event name is not modeled as a separate effect.
issues.reason: The derived contract REF-022 was established from the cross-view fact that the NL's 'Reached Cruising/Cruise' notation separates a trigger from an effect. The FCSTM models the entire string as a trigger with no effect on transition:line:16.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The 'Reached Cruising/Cruise' notation follows the same pattern as 'Closed/SendDeparted': the text after the slash may be part of the event name rather than a separate effect. The compiler consistently models all slash-notation strings as single triggers without effects. If this is the intended interpretation, no effect is missing.
issues.title: Accelerating-to-Cruising transition lacks the required Cruise effect

issues.requirement_quote: If the system is in the Accelerating substate and approaches its destination, it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the "Approached/Decelerate" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Same interpretation as REF-022: the slash notation may represent a single event name. The compiler consistently applies this interpretation across all transitions.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL explicitly states 'The system starts in the DoorsClosing state.' The FCSTM's sole root-scope initial edge (transition:line:34) targets the compiler-owned synthetic state UnspecifiedInitial, not DoorsClosing. No edge from [*] to DoorsClosing exists in the root scope, and verify_facts confirm DoorsClosing is unreachable. The strongest rebuttal—that the FCSTM lowering 'intentionally deferred initial entry' via a synthetic placeholder—is not supported by any exact NL terminal clause, formal edge, or supplied fact establishing that UnspecifiedInitial is an intentional design choice. The NL names DoorsClosing unambiguously as the start state, defeating the synthetic-interpretation alternative.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The root composite must have an unconditional initial edge from [*] to DoorsClosing, making it the system's starting state.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL contract requires the Approaching state to be retained 'while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.' The exact FCSTM facts show the Approaching state (line:14) has two outgoing transitions: line:21 (trigger Arrived_Stop_SendArrived) and line:24 (trigger Obstacle_Detected), both with no guards. The factual absence of a retention guard is clear. However, the NL could be read as describing the semantic exit conditions that the events themselves encode: 'Arrived' implies the system is ready to stop, and 'Obstacle_Detected' is an emergency override that takes precedence over any retention condition. This alternative reading, where the event semantics satisfy the retention constraint without requiring an explicit guard, remains compatible with the supplied facts and constitutes a surviving undercutting defeater.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The NL phrase 'until it is ready to stop or decelerate' describes the natural semantic condition that the triggering events themselves satisfy (Arrived_Stop_SendArrived implies arrival and readiness to stop; Obstacle_Detected is an emergency override), rather than requiring an explicit guard clause on the exit transitions; in this reading, the event semantics subsume the retention condition without a separate guard being necessary.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The system must remain in the Approaching state while the 'nearing destination' condition holds; exit should be constrained by the retention condition 'until it is ready to stop or decelerate'.

semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL states 'If the system is in the Accelerating substate and approaches its destination, it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the Approached/Decelerate signal.' The clause 'approaches its destination' is a guard condition independent of the trigger. The FCSTM transition:line:17 has guard=null. The S5 predicate could not evaluate because the natural-language guard 'approaches its destination' is not in FCSTM logical-expression grammar—this is a W boundary (predicate input format), not a semantic ambiguity. The strongest rebuttal—that 'the event/trigger carrier is a different typed field and cannot satisfy the independent guard'—actually confirms the violation: the trigger (Approached_Decelerate) is semantically distinct from the guard condition (approaches its destination), and no guard is present. The NL's 'and approaches its destination' is a precondition on the state of the world, not a property of the event.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The exact Accelerating to Approaching alternative must retain the independent guard 'approaches its destination'.
